advisory.finding: The implicit Jira DIG project default is removed UNCONDITIONALLY (not gated by the REBAR_RECONCILER_WRITE_FACADE / AC6 rollback toggle), so a deployment whose JIRA_PROJECT / jira.project was previously unset — a previously-valid config that silently resolved to "DIG" — now fails closed on the write path, live probe, runtime scope, and create-time default with no rollback path. dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Verify bind_operation_runtime actually builds the transport from the composed runtime's captured scope in production rather than always forwarding the ambient _load_acli transport into build_backend's test-seam branch.
evidence: reconcile_helpers.py:642 `loader = getattr(ctx.applier, "_load_acli", None)`
reconcile_helpers.py:674-676 `transport = _resolve_pass_transport(ctx)` then `backend = runtime.build_backend(transport=transport)`
applier.py:200 `def _load_acli():` is a module-level function, so getattr on the applier module always returns a callable and _resolve_pass_transport returns the ambient transport
runtime.py:147 `if transport is None:` — build_backend only constructs the real provider transport when transport is None, so a non-None ambient transport bypasses captured-scope construction
commit message claims apply 'resolves the provider transport/scope ONCE per pass (captured at compose time) rather than re-resolving config ambiently per operation'
dropped.finding: bind_operation_runtime resolves the transport via the applier's ambient _load_acli seam and forwards it to build_backend(transport=...); since _load_acli always exists as a module attribute and returns the ambient transport in production, build_backend always takes its test-seam branch (transport is not None) and the composed runtime NEVER builds the real provider transport from captured scope. The transport still originates from ambient config resolution, defeating the AC1 goal of resolving scope once at compose time.
scenarios: Any production reconcile pass with the facade ON (default)
